symptom.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by a full major depressive episode accompanied by delusions and/or hallucinations that are present only during the mood episode. The psychotic content is often mood-congruent (e.g., themes of guilt, worthlessness, or deserved punishment) and can significantly worsen impairment and risk, including suicidality. The course may be single-episode or recurrent, frequently associated with severe functional decline in work, self-care, and relationships, and it often presents subacutely rather than as a sudden break. It is distinguished from primary psychotic disorders by the absence of psychosis outside depressive episodes and from bipolar disorder by the lack of manic or hypomanic episodes.

patient.stressor: Peter’s difficulties began after a back injury on a volunteer fire call led to chronic pain and ultimately forced him to stop most handyman work about a year ago, sharply cutting the household income. At first he tried to fill his time with gardening, soccer, and home-brewing, but as medical bills accumulated and he worried about his wife carrying the financial load, he gradually withdrew from league games and community events, spending more time alone in the garage and avoiding conversations about money. Over seven months, his preoccupation with unpaid bills and the possibility of losing their home deepened to the point that he stopped opening mail and insisted that the bank and utility companies were sending him hidden messages of blame and judgment. His wife finally convinced him to seek psychiatric help after he refused to attend their book club because he was sure neighbors were "in on" a plan to expose him as a failure and he admitted he was terrified to answer the phone or leave the house.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep hearing the bank and bill collectors talking about me, like they’re sending me messages that I’ve ruined everything, even when no one else hears anything.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m convinced the bank and the power company have some kind of file on me and are working together to shame us, like every letter or notice is secretly them pointing out what a useless provider I am, even when my wife shows me it’s just a regular bill.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: A lot of the time when I’m in the house or out in the garage, I hear these clear voices that sound like people from the bank or bill collectors saying things like, “You’ve ruined your family” or “Everyone knows you’re a fraud,” but when I ask my wife if she hears it, she looks at me like I’m crazy because there’s nothing there.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like there’s no point to anything anymore and I’ve already failed my wife and myself, and it just hangs over me from morning until I finally fall asleep.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to get excited about tending the garden or brewing a new batch of beer, but now I just stare at the tools or the empty carboys and feel nothing, so I end up sitting in the garage doing nothing for hours.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I hardly ever feel hungry anymore and usually just pick at whatever my wife puts in front of me, sometimes going most of the day without eating because my stomach feels tied in knots and food just doesn’t seem worth the effort.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Even simple things like getting up from the couch or walking to the kitchen feel like I’m moving through mud, and my wife will ask me something and I just sit there for a long time trying to find the words because everything in my body and head feels slowed down.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how much I lie in bed or nap during the day, I still feel completely drained, like my limbs are made of concrete and just taking a shower or putting on clean clothes can wipe me out for the rest of the afternoon.

add_requirements.delusions_and_hallucinations_occur_exclu: I never had these voices or ideas about the bank and bills targeting me back when I was working and feeling more like myself; they only started after months of feeling deeply down, worthless, and stuck at home with the money problems weighing on me every day.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve basically stopped handling our finances, going to community events, or even answering the phone, and most days I just sit in the garage avoiding people and letting my wife shoulder all the bills and household responsibilities because I feel too ashamed and scared to deal with anything.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, this heavy depression and the scary messages I think I’m getting from the bank and collectors have been going on for about seven months, ever since it became clear my back injury meant I couldn’t keep up with my handyman work and the bills started piling up.
